1. **The role of APOE ε4 in modulating the relationship between non-genetic risk factors and dementia: a system review and meta-analysis.**
   Authors: Xiao-Tong Huang, Liang-Yu Huang, Chen-Chen Tan, Jie-Mei Wei, Xin-Hao Zhang, Lan Tan, Wei Xu
   Journal: Journal of neurology
   Year: 2025
   URL: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41083880/
   Abstract: The ε4 allele of the apolipoprotein E gene (APOE ε4) is the strongest genetic risk factor for dementia. However, it remains unclear whether APOE ε4 status modulates the associations of non-genetic risk factors and dementia risk. This study aims to comprehensively evaluate...

2. **The role of statins in dementia or Alzheimer's disease incidence: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.**
   Authors: Ye Du, Zhangjie Yu, Chengyi Li, Yanxing Zhang, Buyun Xu
   Journal: Frontiers in pharmacology
   Year: 2025
   URL: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39963242/
   Abstract: The effect of statins on the risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease (AD) is unclear.

3. **Statin use and risk of dementia or Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.**
   Authors: Elena Olmastroni, Giulia Molari, Noemi De Beni, Ornella Colpani, Federica Galimberti, Marta Gazzotti, Alberto Zambon, Alberico L Catapano, Manuela Casula
   Journal: European journal of preventive cardiology
   Year: 2022
   URL: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34871380/
   Abstract: As the potential impact of statins on cognitive decline and dementia is still debated, we conducted a meta-analysis of observational studies to examine the effect of statin use on the risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and dementia.

4. **Nonocular Influencing Factors for Primary Glaucoma: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analysis.**
   Authors: Wenman Li, Jiaxing Pan, Maoling Wei, Zhiqing Lv, Sijie Chen, Yang Qin, Ni Li
   Journal: Ophthalmic research
   Year: 2022
   URL: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34517373/
   Abstract: Glaucoma is the main cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. Still, little is known about nonocular risk factors. We use an umbrella review to examine the meta-analytic evidence of the correlation between nonocular factors and glaucoma.
